headline: Protein language models diverge from natural language in layerwise information use
label: Protein Language Model Mechanisms
summary: Mechanistic and architectural analyses now probe how protein language models process repeats and layers, moving beyond sequence scoring.
synthesis: The common thread across these items is treating biological sequence language models as objects whose internal computation is analyzed or modified, rather than only as scorers. One preprint compares how information is distributed across transformer attention layers in protein and natural language models and uses that comparison to adapt early-exit inference. A second is a mechanistic interpretability study showing that protein language models detect exact and approximate repeats through positional heads and amino-acid similarity. The codon-level SynCodonLM is related but distinct: it masks non-synonymous codons before the softmax and clusters codons by nucleotide properties, and it outperforms baselines on its evaluation tasks. What is new is the shift toward protein-specific representations and architectural choices, with learned internal representations becoming the primary object of study.
